claimVersions.text: There exist absolute C > 0 and an integer n_0 such that alpha(n) <= C f(n) for every integer n >= n_0.
For an absolute c > 0, the integers n >= 5 with c f(n) <= alpha(n) have natural density 1; c is chosen independently of all n and cutoffs.
For fixed positive absolute c and C, the simultaneous inequalities c f(n) <= alpha(n) <= C f(n) hold on a set of positive integers of natural density 1.
There exist a,A > 0 and X_0 > 4 such that a f(X) <= max_{1<=n<X} alpha(n) <= A f(X) for every real X >= X_0.
For X >= 0, realGoodInputs c C X consists exactly of the integers n with 5 <= n <= X satisfying both non-strict bounds.
A density-zero count of orderExceptions is equivalent to the density-one goodInputs proportion, and the natural-cutoff good proportion gives the same real-cutoff proportion.
For X > 1, maximumBelow X is the maximum of alpha(n) over exactly the positive integers n < X.
